info.name: Middleware Third-Party Service
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Middleware Third-Party Service.

This service manages third-party provider integrations, client access control, and API execution gateway.

## Setup Flow
1. Create Providers
2. Create Provider APIs
3. Configure Environment (URLs, credentials)
4. Create Clients
5. Grant Provider Access to Clients
6. Grant API Access to Clients
7. Execute APIs via Gateway

## Authentication
- Admin endpoints: JWT Bearer token (Keycloak)
- Execution endpoint: Client secretKey (no JWT needed)

item.name: 3. Environment Configs
item.description:
Configure API environment settings (base URLs, credentials, headers per environment).

Each API can have separate DEV and PROD configs with different base URLs and credentials.

request.description: List all environment configs (DEV, PROD) for a specific API.

item.name: 4. Clients
item.description: Manage API clients (internal services or external partners that consume third-party APIs through the gateway).

body.raw:
{
    "name": "Lending Service",
    "code": "LENDING_SERVICE",
    "description": "Lending service client for credit checks and IBAN verification",
    "callbackUrl": "http://lending-service:8091/api/v1/callbacks",
    "environment": "DEV",
    "ipWhitelist": []
}

request.description:
Create a new API client.

Environment: DEV, PROD, or BOTH
- DEV: Client can only call DEV environment APIs
- PROD: Client can only call PROD environment APIs
- BOTH: Client can call both
- TEST: Client gets mock responses (no real HTTP calls)

The response includes a generated secretKey. Save it — the client uses it to authenticate when executing APIs.
Regenerate the client's secretKey. The old key is immediately invalidated.

item.name: 5. Client Access (Provider + API Assignment)
item.description:
Grant or revoke access for a client to providers and their specific APIs.

This is the core assignment flow:
1. Grant Provider Access — allows the client to use a provider
2. Grant API Access — allows the client to call a specific API within that provider

Both are required for execution to work.

item.name: Provider Access
item.description: Grant/revoke/list provider-level access for a client.

request.description:
Grant a client access to a provider.

targetId = the provider's UUID
environment = DEV, PROD, or BOTH

You must call this ONCE per provider you want the client to use.
List all providers this client has been granted access to.
Revoke a client's access to a provider.

item.name: API Access
item.description: Grant/revoke/list API-level access for a client.

request.description:
Grant a client access to a specific API.

targetId = the API's UUID (from provider-apis)
environment = DEV, PROD, or BOTH

You must call this ONCE per API you want the client to use.
List all APIs this client has been granted access to (across all providers).

List APIs this client can access for a specific provider.

Useful to see: 'Which SIMAH APIs does this client have?'

item.name: Bulk Access
item.description: Grant access to multiple providers and their APIs in a single call.

request.description:
Grant access to multiple providers and their APIs in one call.

Send an array of providers, each with an array of API IDs.
Inserts into both client_provider_access and client_api_access tables.
Skips any that already exist.

Returns counts of providers and APIs granted.

item.name: 6. Execute API (Gateway)
item.description:
Execute third-party API calls through the middleware gateway.

No JWT required — authentication is via client secretKey.

The gateway:
1. Authenticates client by secretKey
2. Checks idempotency
3. Verifies API access
4. Routes to mock (TEST) or live (DEV/PROD)
5. Applies auth credentials from env config
6. Logs request and response

request.description:
Execute a third-party API call.

The apiCode in the URL path is the API's unique code (e.g., SIMAH_SCORE_CREDIT, NAFATH_INITIATE, UNIFONIC_SEND_OTP).

Authentication is via secretKey in the request body (NOT JWT).

The requestBody field is a JSON string that will be forwarded to the third-party API.

Simplified execution endpoint.

Secret key goes in X-Secret-Key header instead of request body.
The request body is sent directly to the third-party API (no wrapper).
Execute with idempotency key. If the same key is used again, the cached response is returned instead of making a new call.

item.name: 7. Request Logs
item.description: View API execution logs. Every API call is logged with request/response details.

request.description: Look up a log by the requestId returned from the execute endpoint.

item.name: 8. Callbacks
item.description: View callback responses from async third-party API calls (e.g., Nafath, IVR).
